create.name: Mirabai Starr
create.bio:
Mirabai Starr is an author and teacher of interspiritual contemplative practice who lives in the mountains of northern New Mexico. Born in New York in 1961 and raised partly in Taos, she spent her teenage years at the Lama Foundation, a community open to many faiths, and later spent twenty years lecturing on religion and philosophy at the Taos campus of the University of New Mexico. She first became known for fresh English versions of the Spanish mystics Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross, and has since written Wild Mercy, on the women mystics; God of Love, on the common heart of Judaism, Christianity and Islam; the memoir Caravan of No Despair; and Ordinary Mysticism (2024).

Her teaching draws on the poetry and lives of mystics from many paths, with a particular eye on the sacred feminine and on loss as a doorway to the holy, a theme shaped by the death of her daughter Jenny in 2001. Gatherings mix readings, silence, sung divine names in several languages, conversation and writing used as a spiritual practice. With the artist Willow Brook she runs Wild Heart, the online home of her membership The Mystic's Way, short self-paced writing journeys and a yearly writing retreat in Mexico, and she leads weekend programmes at Esalen in Big Sur.

books.title: Wild Mercy: Living the Fierce and Tender Wisdom of the Women Mystics
books.author: Mirabai Starr
books.description: Her most widely read book, published by Sounds True in 2019. It gathers women mystics, saints and goddess figures from many traditions and asks what their courage and compassion can offer readers of any gender today.

books.title: Ordinary Mysticism: Your Life as Sacred Ground
books.author: Mirabai Starr
books.description: A 2024 book from HarperOne arguing that direct experience of the sacred belongs to everyday life rather than to temples and clergy. Stories from her own life sit beside lessons from teachers across the centuries, with practices and writing prompts.

books.title: God of Love: A Guide to the Heart of Judaism, Christianity and Islam
books.author: Mirabai Starr
books.description: An award-winning look at the teachings that the three Abrahamic faiths hold in common, told through saints, prophets and the author's own experiences. A revised edition followed in 2026.

books.title: Caravan of No Despair: A Memoir of Loss and Transformation
books.author: Mirabai Starr
books.description: A memoir of growing up in the counterculture and of the years after her teenage daughter was killed in a car accident, on the day her first translation came out. It mixes personal story, humour and reflections drawn from the mystics.

books.title: Dark Night of the Soul
books.author: John of the Cross; translated by Mirabai Starr
books.description: Her modern English translation of the sixteenth-century Spanish poem and its prose commentary, with her own introduction. The text follows the soul's passage through darkness towards union with the divine.

books.title: Teresa of Avila: The Book of My Life
books.author: Teresa of Avila; translated by Mirabai Starr
books.description: A fresh translation of the Spanish saint's autobiography, published by Shambhala. Plain, lively English mirrors the everyday voice in which Teresa described her prayer life and visions.

courses.title: The Mystic's Way: Your Life as Sacred Ground
courses.description: A weekend at Esalen in Big Sur on the common ground shared by the world's mystical paths. Days bring together readings from mystic poets and scriptures, sitting in silence, chanting divine names in many languages, and group conversation and writing. People of any faith, several faiths or none are welcome.

courses.title: The Mystic's Way: Living Wisdom Across the Spiritual Traditions
courses.description: An ongoing online membership built on twelve themes, from interspirituality and service to death and creativity, each opened up through the stories of mystics and mythic figures. Members receive a weekly video teaching, writing prompts and a monthly live question session with Mirabai. Enrolment opens a few times a year.
courses.price: $59 USD per month or $399 USD per year

courses.title: Embodied Writing: A 7-Day Practice
courses.description: A self-paced week of writing as contemplative practice. Each day brings a chosen poem, a short video from Mirabai and a prompt, and the material stays with you to repeat.

courses.title: Holy Wanting: Reclaiming Feminine Wisdom
courses.description: A seven-day self-paced journey by email and video on desire as something sacred rather than an obstacle. Daily themes move from the earth and the world's sorrows to justice, the arts and longing for the divine, each with a writing prompt.

courses.title: Wild Heart Writing Retreat in Bacalar
courses.description: Six days by the lagoon at Bacalar on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula given to writing as a spiritual path, with small sharing circles, morning movement, chanting and meditation. The group also spends a day writing at a Mayan archaeological site.
courses.price: From $4,500 USD (early-bird from $4,000 USD), shared room

free_resources.title: Sabbath Notes from Mirabai
free_resources.description: A free YouTube series of short reflections on keeping a weekly day of sacred rest, filmed as she practises it herself.

sprint.tier_override: Owner confirmed (1 Nov 2026). luminary by editorial stature: a major author in her field, with more than a dozen books including widely used translations of Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross (Riverhead, Shambhala), Wild Mercy (Sounds True) and Ordinary Mysticism (HarperOne); named on the 2020 Watkins list of the 100 most spiritually influential living people. Readable follower counts alone would give local_hero.
flags: No email is published on mirabaistarr.com or wildheart.space; the contact form is used. Her contact page says she is currently declining most speaking invitations to focus on writing.

Grief and loss are a large part of her public teaching (Holy Lament membership, grief clips, bereavement counselling credential); grief-led items were left out to stay clear of the condition rule, while her main work on mysticism was kept. A human may want to confirm.

She is in docs/content-audits/the-shift-network-faculty.json (six courses, activity 'older') and her programs page links to two Shift on-demand courses, but Shift course pages returned 403 to curl and no current Shift programme was confirmed, so the-shift-network is not added to teaches_at.
Wild Heart is co-run with Willow Brook; The Mystic's Way, Embodied Writing, Holy Wanting and the Bacalar retreat are all taught by Mirabai on that platform.
The wildheart.space pages carry leftover web-developer notes in visible text (instructions on where to paste footer code); not addressed to readers and ignored.
Second photo is her older black-and-white YouTube avatar; clearly the same person as the 2025 Esalen portrait, though some years younger.
